title: Redis
subtitle: Read hot data. Analyze it with SQL.
intro: Query Redis strings, hashes and lists from DuckDB, or snapshot operational data into local tables for analysis. Every Redis call selects a named DuckDB secret, keeping connection details separate from the data-access expression.

reference.name: redis_get(key, secret)
reference.description: Read a string (NULL when missing); redis_set writes one.

reference.name: redis_hget(key, field, secret)
reference.description: Read one hash field; redis_hset writes and returns fields added.

reference.name: redis_hgetall(key, secret)
reference.description: Field and value rows; redis_hgetall_map returns one MAP per row.

reference.name: redis_lrange_list(key, start, stop, secret)
reference.description: A list slice as VARCHAR[]; 0, -1 is the whole list.

reference.name: redis_mget_list(keys, secret)
reference.description: Typed MGET: a VARCHAR[] of values, NULL for each missing key.

reference.name: redis_scan_page(cursor, pattern, count, secret)
reference.description: One SCAN step as STRUCT(cursor, keys); repeat until the cursor is '0'.

reference.name: redis_hscan_over_scan(pattern, fields, n, secret)
reference.description: Stream key, field and value rows from matching hashes.

reference.name: redis_command(['INCR', 'hits'], secret)
reference.description: Run any other command; arrays return as JSON, nil as NULL.

notes.title: Choose table-shaped results
notes.body: Prefer the typed _list, _page and _map functions: values containing commas or empty strings stay unambiguous. The older redis_mget, redis_lrange and redis_scan return comma-separated strings. Wrap redis_get or redis_hget in coalesce for a default.

notes.title: Scope scans and connections
notes.body: Key listing uses SCAN, never KEYS, but redis_keys and redis_hscan_over_scan walk every page; narrow the pattern on large keyspaces. Each reply wait is bounded by redis_timeout_ms (30 s) or the secret’s timeout_ms. Connections are pooled per secret, and every function refuses while enable_external_access is false.

examples.title: Name the connection
examples.caption: username, password, db and timeout_ms are optional. Creating the secret does not connect.

examples.title: Read a hash as rows
examples.caption: Requires the server and a Redis hash at user:42.
examples.reason: Connects to Redis and reads an existing hash.

examples.title: Snapshot matching hashes
examples.caption: Use a pattern containing only hashes. Subsequent analysis reads the local snapshot.
examples.reason: Requires a running Redis server and matching hash keys.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM duckdb_secrets() WHERE name = 'quickref_redis' AND type = 'redis') THEN true ELSE error('Redis secret was not created') END;
